message.oldrepublic.story.c4.price: A small droid drops out of the clouds, sweeps you with red light, chirps twice and climbs away.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.seeker.jedi: Master Saelen will want to hear about this.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.seeker.sith: Overseer Sorn will want to hear about this.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.seeker.inde: The journal stirs. Read it at Courier's Fall.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.nav_log: The wreck's nav log names two worlds, Selvaren and Varkhast, and a spot nearby where Vasch laid up a spare courier under a tarp.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.hulk: The courier lies under its tarp nearby. Your journal marks it.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.salvage: Your Sense finds a hyperdrive motivator still in its cradle among the wreckage.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.salvage_aga: Among the wreckage, a second motivator. Someone kept spares.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.motivator_f: In the poachers' cache: the freighter's hyperdrive motivator, wrapped in old sacking.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.compass_hum: The Compass hums. Tessaly Arn's road starts near here.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.not_now: The expedition will wait in the journal.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.slot_full: %s waits for a free slot. Open the skills screen and free one.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.speed_refun: Tessaly returns the %s skill points you spent on Force Speed. Her teaching is a gift.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.relic: Behind the crypt's seal: a relic of the old dead. Bring it to the Proving.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.trial.heart: The Heartstone wakes. Keep the corruption back.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.trial.sepul: The Sepulchre's doors grind open behind you.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.trial.left: You left the trial. It will begin again when you return.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.crystal: The crystal settles in your palm, warm and attuned to you.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.clue.1: A clue: a name on a datapad, Torvin Kaast. (%s/%s)
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.clue.2: A clue: Kaast took the contract from someone else, a buyer who pays in Core credits. (%s/%s)
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.clue.3: A clue: a sealed contract signed only "the Buyer". (%s/%s)
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.sabotage: As the ship settles, a charge in the landing strut blows. Three claw scratches are burned into the ramp.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.peaceful_cl: A hunter's drone left this, tucked into your pack while you slept.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.ambush.1: Jet packs whine overhead. Mandalorian hunters are dropping in.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.ambush.2: Hunters again, and something heavy and metal walking with them.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.ambush.fled: The hunters lose your trail. They will try again.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.bounty: A lone hunter has found you. There is a contract on your head.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.beacon: A marker beacon thuds into the ground nearby, pulsing red. It carries a recorded voice.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.beacon_othe: This beacon was not left for you.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.peaceful_du: Kaast walks into the camp with his hands open. He wants to talk.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.ending.spar: Kaast takes off his helmet, names the Buyer's broker, "a Hutt's factor in the Core, no more than that", and leaves his armour pattern as a debt paid.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.ending.stri: Kaast strips the plate. "Wear it better than I did." He walks into the waste.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.ending.end: A short, unshowy end. His rifle lies on the ground.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.stash: Kaast's stash: what he carried for a long hunt.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.helper_rewa: You helped bring down Torvin Kaast.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.rematch_don: Kaast is licking his wounds. Come back tomorrow.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.complete: Chapter Four is complete. Every destination is open.
message.oldrepublic.story.c4.back_pay: Back pay for your deeds on the frontier: %s credits.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.c4.brief.archive: The Archive kept Selvaren's coordinates; I have written them in your journal. The Patient Star lies under her tarp near here. Make her fly.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.c4.brief.memory: I have no star charts any more, so I give you Selvaren from memory. I walked its forests once, when the Watch still had a home there.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.c4.lift_off: She flies. The Patient Star was always more stubborn than her name. Selvaren is waiting.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.c4.report.spare: You let him go, and he paid you in truth. Mercy bought us a name. Remember that it can.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.c4.report.strip: You took his armour and left him his life. A hard kindness, but a kindness.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.c4.report.end: He would have done the same to you. I know. I still wish it had gone another way.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.c4.brief: The courier is yours. Make it fly and take it to Varkhast. If it falls out of the sky, I will requisition another pilot.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.c4.lift_off: It flies. Good. Varkhast, then. Kaddor keeps lists, and you are on one now.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.c4.report.spare: You let a hunter walk away. He will remember that, and so will everyone who hires him. Use it.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.c4.report.strip: You took his plate and his pride. That is a lesson he will carry for the rest of his short life.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.c4.report.end: Clean. The next hunter will think twice about the contract. That is the point.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.name: Tessaly Arn
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c4.leave: You were always going to leave.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c4.lift_off: Listen to her engines. That is what a road sounds like.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c4.report.spare: You let him go. Roads cross twice, more often than you would think.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c4.report.strip: He will walk lighter now. So will you.
npc.oldrepublic.ansa.name: Keeper Ansa Veylin
npc.oldrepublic.ansa.c4.welcome: Welcome to the Greenwatch. Mind the garden.
npc.oldrepublic.ansa.c4.welcome_wary: You are served here. Do not mistake that for welcome.
npc.oldrepublic.ansa.c4.heartstone_teach: Stand still. Let nothing through. The stone has always known how; now so do you.
npc.oldrepublic.kaddor.name: Overseer Vael Kaddor
npc.oldrepublic.kaddor.c4.welcome: The Proving. Try not to embarrass Sorn.
npc.oldrepublic.kaddor.c4.welcome_wary: The Order's student. You will be watched.
npc.oldrepublic.zarvos.name: Lord Hadrek Zarvos
npc.oldrepublic.zarvos.c4.rise: Another thief at my door. Come, then. Come down to me.
npc.oldrepublic.zarvos.c4.take_it: You want what I had? Take it from me.
npc.oldrepublic.kaast.name: Torvin Kaast
npc.oldrepublic.hunter.name: Mandalorian hunter
npc.oldrepublic.smuggler.name: Jory Tal, smuggler
dialogue.oldrepublic.officer_republic.op: I need to requisition supplies.
dialogue.oldrepublic.officer_imperial.op: I need to requisition supplies.
dialogue.oldrepublic.officer_republic.op: Do you know where I could find a hyperdrive motivator?
dialogue.oldrepublic.officer_imperial.op: Do you know where I could find a hyperdrive motivator?
journal.oldrepublic.entry.a_price.title: A Price
journal.oldrepublic.entry.a_price.body: A seeker droid came down out of the clouds and swept me with red light. Someone wanted to know what I look like up close. Someone has put a price on me.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_patient_st: Saelen knew the droid's make: a Mandalorian hunter's. She gave me the Watch's old courier, the Patient Star, asleep under a tarp since before the Treaty, and a world to fly her to.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.a_written_off_: Sorn has requisitioned a courier the Empire wrote off. Four parts and a pilot who does not die, he says, and then Varkhast, where the Empire keeps its oldest dead.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.vaschs_courier: At Courier's Fall the wreck's nav log named two worlds and a spot nearby where Vasch laid up a spare courier. Tessaly's voice came through the Compass: "You were always going to leave."
journal.oldrepublic.entry.a_trade.title: A Trade
journal.oldrepublic.entry.a_trade.body: I chose a trade at the Engineering Bench. Whatever else I am, now I can make things.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.a_part_off_the: A smuggler pointed me at a crashed freighter and the poachers squatting on it. The motivator was in their cache. Nobody will ask where it came from.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_ship_flies: Four parts fitted, the tarp pulled back, the running lights on. She flies.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.selvaren.title: Selvaren
journal.oldrepublic.entry.selvaren.body: Selvaren: high forests, still tarns, and an old enclave in a clearing, the Greenwatch. The Watch's first home.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.varkhast.title: Varkhast
journal.oldrepublic.entry.varkhast.body: Varkhast: red rock and falling ash, and an academy outpost against a cliff, the Proving. The Empire keeps its dead here.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_greenwatch: Two soured waystones cleansed for Keeper Ansa. The corruption is spreading from the Heartstone itself.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_heartstone: I stood in the Heartstone's ring while the corruption came in waves, and the stone taught me to stand still and let nothing through. Force Barrier.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_singing_ho: A grotto where the crystals sing. I pushed the stones in the order they hummed, and at the bottom a crystal answered me.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_proving.bo: A relic brought up from a greater tomb, past the diggers and the dead. Kaddor wrote my name down.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.zarvos_sepulch: Lord Hadrek Zarvos seized me in his own tomb and told me to take what he had. I took it. Force Choke.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_rift.title: The Rift
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_rift.body: Down the black-glass ledges of the duskglass rift, to a crystal I held while the rift whispered. It bled red in my hand.
Tessaly Arn's echo led me to a Wayfarer cache and taught me to walk the long road quickly. Force Speed.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.both_doors.bod: I did a favour for a hub that does not count me as its own. Doors stay open that way.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.two_blades.bod: Two crystals, one hilt. I built a saberstaff.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.sabotage.title: Sabotage
journal.oldrepublic.entry.sabotage.body: When my ship landed at home a charge in the landing strut blew. Three claw scratches burned into the ramp, and a datapad with a name: Torvin Kaast.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.first_ambush.b: Mandalorian hunters dropped on me out of the sky. The last one yielded: the contract was never theirs. Kaast took it from a buyer who pays in Core credits.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_buyer.body: The hunters' droid carried a sealed contract, signed only "the Buyer". Someone far from the frontier wants me found.
A marker beacon, a recorded voice. Torvin Kaast has made camp and invited me to it.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.kaast_spared.b: I let Kaast go. He named the Buyer's broker, a factor in the Core, and left me his armour pattern as a debt paid.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.kaast_stripped: I took Kaast's armour. "Wear it better than I did," he said, and walked into the waste.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.kaast_ended.bo: I ended Torvin Kaast. His rifle is mine now.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.report_c4.body: I told my mentor how the hunt ended. Every world on the charts is open to me now.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.bounty_hunters: Hunters work the frontier for whoever pays. The good ones send a seeker droid ahead to learn the size of the job before they quote a price.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.selvaren.title: Selvaren
journal.oldrepublic.codex.selvaren.body: A forest world of highwood, meadow and tarn. The Watch kept its first home here, around a great waystone called the Heartstone.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.varkhast.title: Varkhast
journal.oldrepublic.codex.varkhast.body: A world of red rock and ash. The Empire buries its oldest dead in greater tombs here and tests its students against them at the Proving.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.the_watch_on_s: Before the frontier, the Watch kept stones that hum. The Greenwatch is what is left of its first enclave, and Keeper Ansa Veylin keeps it still.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.the_proving_co: Every Imperial academy sends its best to the Proving once. They walk down into the tombs; those who walk out are given a rank.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.force_speed.bo: The Force carries the body faster than legs alone. A burst can close a gap or open one. Tessaly called it walking the long road quickly.
A wall of stillness the Force holds around you. Bolts stop against it; a big enough blow breaks it.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.force_choke.bo: The Force closes a throat from a distance. It works only on what breathes, and it marks whoever uses it.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.mandalorians.b: Clans of warriors who sell their skill. Jet packs, wrist flamers, rockets, nets, and armour handed down like a name.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.security_droid: Heavy walkers that shrug off blaster fire and cannot be choked. A shock or a blade finds their seams.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.hollowhorns.bo: Selvaren's grazing beasts: calm until struck or until a calf is threatened, then a charge that can stun against a wall.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.ash_hounds.bod: Varkhast's pack hunters. They flank, they lunge, and a well-timed parry turns the lunge.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.disciplines.bo: Armstech, Armourcraft, Artifice and Medtech: the trades of the Engineering Bench. A crafter learns two, and grows in each by making things.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.credits.title: Credits
journal.oldrepublic.codex.credits.body: Chits and bundles of a hundred. Contracts, enemies and vendors deal in them; a vendor changes chits for bundles and back.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.starships.body: A courier needs a hull, a power core, a hyperdrive motivator and a nav computer, and fuel cells to jump. Damage it badly enough and it will not jump at all.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.the_buyer.body: Someone in the Core pays for my trail through brokers and factors. The contract carries no name, only "the Buyer".
journal.oldrepublic.codex.torvin_kaast.b: A Mandalorian tracker of long reputation. He took the contract on me from the Buyer and came himself, to measure what he was hunting.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_call_saelen.kaas: Kaast named a Hutt's factor. Here he is.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_call_saelen.call: The Watch still has friends among the Outer Rim's harbourmasters. Three of them have seen the same man this month: a Hutt's factor, asking after "a frontier Jedi who makes stones sing".
Whoever hired the Mandalorian has not given up. They have only changed their tools. The factor keeps his books at Saltgate, a Hutt port on Ghessar. Go and find out why.
Why would anyone want me alive?
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_call_saelen.why: A hunter is paid for a body. A factor is paid for a delivery. Someone wants you whole, and that frightens me more than any price on your head. Ghessar's coordinates are in your ship's nav. Take the helm yourself if you can; you will need the practice.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_call_sorn.kaast: Kaast named a Hutt's factor. Here he is.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_call_sorn.call: Someone is spending a fortune on you, and spending it through a Hutt.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_call_sorn.call2: That is the question, is it not? The coin passes through a factor at Saltgate, a port on Ghessar where the Hutts keep the business they would rather not see. Find out who, and whether they are worth killing.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_call_sorn.opt.wh: Why not kill the factor and be done with it?
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_call_sorn.why: Because a dead factor is a closed ledger. Read it first. Then do what you like with the man who kept it. The coordinates are in your ship. Fly her yourself; an apprentice who cannot hold a helm is cargo.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_hub_saelen.repor: The storms over Tyrvann have a different voice tonight. Quieter. Tell me what you found in the Hymnal, and what you did there.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_hub_saelen.opt.r: I spared her. She walked out into the storm, and the engine went quiet behind her.
I bound her. She will answer for what she did, and sing for no one.
I ended her, in the dark beside the engine.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_hub_saelen.idle: Not now. Rest while you can. The Hymn will not.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_hub_sorn.report: The Council has said nothing about Ulvaine for a week, which means it is frightened. You are standing here, which means you are not dead. Tell me what you did.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_hub_sorn.opt.rep: I let her go. She walked into the storm with nothing.
I bound her and delivered her.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_hub_sorn.idle: Do not loiter. Power is not taken by standing still.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_harbourmaster.we: Pad fees waived. Don't thank me, thank the kajidic. The Exalted Vessba likes to know who lands on her sand, and about you, friend, she is very curious.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_harbourmaster.op: Why is she curious about me?
I am looking for a factor. A man who buys things for people far away.
My ship is out in the sand. Can you bring it to a pad?
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_harbourmaster.cu: Because a man in her own port has been asking about you, and paying well to ask. Ommo Teel keeps her accounts and her appointments; talk to him. Or talk to the Mandalorian in the cantina, if you like your answers with a blade in them.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_harbourmaster.fa: That will be Dask. His counting-house is behind the cantina, and he keeps the door shut and his guards awake. There are three ways past a door like that: the kajidic opens it for you, the clan breaks it for you, or you find your own way in.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_harbourmaster.po: Saltgate was a crash site once. Three freighters came down in a sandstorm, and the Hutts bought the wreckage before the crews had finished dying. Everything here is for sale. Mind the enforcers: they keep the peace, and they keep it expensive.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_harbourmaster.gr: The pad is yours as long as you pay or you are interesting. You are still interesting.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.greet: Ommo Teel, majordomo to the Exalted Vessba. You are the one the factor's coin has been chasing. How fortunate that you came to us first.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.opt.jo: What does the kajidic want from me?
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.opt.au: Your jobs are done. I would like that audience.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.jobs: Two small tasks, to show the kajidic you are worth its trouble. A debtor in the canyons owes us a strongbox. And a crate must leave Ghessar's orbit without the clan's patrol counting it. Do both, and the Exalted One will tell you everything the factor would rather she did not.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.jobs_d: One small task, to show the kajidic you are worth its trouble: a debtor in the canyons owes us a strongbox. Bring it, and the Exalted One will tell you everything the factor would rather she did not.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.debt_b: Orvo Plint borrowed against a salvage claim and then sold the salvage. He camps in the canyons with a few friends as desperate as he is. Bring us his strongbox. How you get it is your affair.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.cargo_: A sealed crate goes into your ship's hold the moment you agree. Take it up into orbit and leave it at the nav buoy at the system's edge. Clan Hask flies patrols up there. If they scan you, the crate is theirs and the job is void. If you shoot them, they will remember it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.debt_s: The strongbox is still in the canyons, and so is Plint. The kajidic is patient, but its interest is not.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.opt.dr: I want to drop this job.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.cargo_: The crate is in your hold and the buoy is at the edge of the system. Fly quietly.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.drop_c: Then the job goes back on the ledger. You may take it again when you are ready.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.audien: Then the Exalted One will see you. Approach the dais, and keep your hands where her guards can count them.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.lore: The Vessba kajidic owns Saltgate: the pads, the walls, the water and the debts. Especially the debts. The Exalted One is patient, and patience compounds.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.debt_b: You have the box. Good. Another line of the ledger closes.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.debt_r: You come back with empty hands and a story. I am listening. But the kajidic pays for boxes, not for stories.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.opt.tr: [Mind Trick] The box was empty. You believe me.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.opt.br: It was empty. And here are 150 credits that say so.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.opt.go: You are right. I will go back for it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_majordomo.idle: The Exalted One is not receiving. Come back when you have business with the kajidic.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_vessba.audience: So. The singer comes to Vessba's hall, having done Vessba's chores. Teel says you are useful. Teel is rarely wrong about useful.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_vessba.sell: Imrel Dask. He keeps his ledgers behind my cantina and his secrets behind his teeth, and for a month he has been spending a Sith's money in my port, on you. Dask's coin is good. Mine is better. Go. My guards will be looking at the sky when you pass his door.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_vessba.who: That he will tell you himself. Vessba sells doors, little singer, not what waits behind them.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_vessba.after: The singer returns. Vessba's door stays open to those who keep Vessba's ledger tidy.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_vessba.opt.lore: How does a Hutt come to own a port like this?
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_vessba.lore: Patience. A ship falls, a crew dies, the sand covers everything. Vessba waits, and buys the sand. Everyone who lands here walks on Vessba.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_vessba.greet: Vessba does not speak to strangers. Teel speaks to strangers. Go, and be less strange.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.greet_spar: You let our cousin live. Torvin is a deserter and a fool, but he is ours, and Clan Hask remembers who sent him home breathing. Sit. Drink. Then we talk business.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.opt.why: What does the clan want with the factor?
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.opt.honour: I will answer for Kaast. Name the duel.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.greet_stri: You took Torvin's armour and left him in the waste. He lived, so I will not draw on you. But that helmet is clan iron, forged for his father's father. Bring it back to me.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.greet_end: You are the one who killed Torvin Kaast. He was a deserter, and a fool, and my cousin. Before the clan does business with you, you answer for him: blade to blade, with my champion. Win, and the debt is paid.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.greet: Varra Hask, envoy of Clan Hask. You have the look of someone the Buyer's coin is chasing. In a way, so do we.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.later: The factor's ledger is open, and the witch's name is in it. Clan Hask will not forget who opened it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.why: The Buyer's coin hired our elders to guard a Sith's temple on Tyrvann. The elders took it. The warriors did not. We are hunters, not doorkeepers for a witch. Dask holds the contract; bring him down, and the clan is free of it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.matriarch_: Then hunt like one of us. A sand scour matriarch has been taking salvagers in the dunes. Kill her and her brood, and the clan walks beside you into Dask's counting-house.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.honour_bri: Good. My champion fights with a real blade, and so will you. When one of you yields, it is done. She will wait beside me until you are ready.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.hunt_statu: The matriarch still hunts. Your journal knows the dunes she favours.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.opt.drop: I want to give up the hunt.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.duel_statu: My champion is beside me. Go to her when you are ready to bleed.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.opt.drop_d: Not today. Release me from the duel.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.drop_confi: Then it waits for another day. The clan is patient about honour. Only about honour.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.lore: Clan Hask hunts and flies: a few dozen warriors under my brother Dorrun, camped on Tyrvann where the storm keeps the curious away. We take contracts and we keep our word. Lately our elders have been keeping the wrong one.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_varra.clan_help: The witch's blockade has thrown you back twice now. The clan could fly with you. Fuel and missiles are not free, even for friends: a thousand credits, and my fighters break formation at your side.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_doorman.door: The counting-house is closed. Master Dask sees no one without an appointment, and nobody has an appointment.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_doorman.opt.tric: [Mind Trick] You will open the door, and you will forget my face.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_doorman.opt.fear: [Fear] Look at me. Then look at the door, and decide which frightens you more.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_doorman.after: Whatever happened up there, I did not see it. I never see anything. It is in my contract.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_debtor.plead: You are Teel's, aren't you? Look at this camp. The salvage went on food and fuel, and the kajidic's interest went up every week we ate. That box is all we have left.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_debtor.opt.force: Hand it over, or your friends find out how I fight.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_debtor.opt.pay: I will pay your debt myself. Two hundred credits.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_debtor.opt.run: Take the box and run. I will tell Teel it was empty.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_debtor.gone: Leave us be. There is nothing left here worth taking.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dask.greet: Come in. Close the door, if it still closes. I have been expecting you since the day Kaast failed. I only hoped it would be later.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dask.buyer: Darth Ulvaine. She was a voice on the Dark Council's edges until she started asking for things the Council would not give her. Now she buys them instead, through men like me.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dask.opt.want: What does she want with me?
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dask.want: You, alive. Your Resonance makes stones sing, and the thing she has found under Tyrvann's storms needs a singer. She was very clear about "alive". She was less clear about the rest of you.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dask.holo_1: The desk projector paints a tall woman in blue light, hooded, very still. Her voice is calm: "Dask. Kaast has failed me, and his clan sits on my sky, taking my coin. Find me the frontier child who hears the stone."
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dask.holo_2: "Alive, Dask. A dead singer is only meat, and the Hymn needs a throat. Until the singer arrives, Tyrvann's sky is closed." The figure bows its head and is gone.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dask.coords: That is all of it. Tyrvann's coordinates, and the pattern her blockade flies: take them. They were always going to end up with you. Now. What happens to me?
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dask.opt.release: Go. Fly out at dawn and do not come back.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dask.opt.clan: Clan Hask wants a word with you. Varra is waiting.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dask.gone: The office is empty. A cold cup of caf sits on the desk beside a ledger with its last page torn out.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dorrun.greet: Huntmaster Dorrun Hask. My sister says you are worth the trouble you bring. The storm says nothing. It never does.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dorrun.opt.recal: My ship is out in the storm. Can you bring it to the pad?
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dorrun.stones: Three of them, sung awake by the witch's people: one in the stormwood, one in the mire, one up on the basalt. They are on your map now. Her Hymnsworn guard each one. Put the guards down, then lay your hand on the stone and make it quiet.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dorrun.hymnal: An old temple in the basalt ridges, where the lightning will not leave the arch alone. The stones sing to it. Silence them and its heart opens. Our elders took the witch's coin to guard whatever she woke in there. I am done guarding it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dorrun.lore: The holdfast keeps the storm off our heads and our fighters dry. The clan has camped here three winters, and the storm has not noticed us yet. One day it will.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_dorrun.cold: The clan serves outsiders at the pad and the board. The huntmaster talks to friends.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_ulvaine_yield.yi: Enough. The song has your measure, singer, and so do I. Choose, and be quick about it. I will not beg.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_ulvaine_yield.op: Go. Walk out into your storm.
The Watch will hold you. Get up.
The Council will want you. Get up.
Clan Hask has a price on you too. Get up.
dialogue.oldrepublic.c5_ulvaine_yield.go: Only the engine's hum is left, and even that is fading.
dialogue.oldrepublic.spindle_log.entry_1: SILENT SPINDLE, STATION LOG. Survey cycle, day 1. The long-range array has caught a tone from Tyrvann. Not a signal: a note, holding steady at the edge of hearing.
dialogue.oldrepublic.spindle_log.entry_2: Day 9. The note has company. Eleven voices, then forty. The techs say it is the storm. The techs have stopped sleeping.
dialogue.oldrepublic.spindle_log.entry_3: Day 14. A ship came up out of the storm. A woman asked us to turn the array off. We said no. She said that was fine. She only needed us to listen.
dialogue.oldrepublic.spindle_log.entry_4: Day 15. Final entry. Everyone is very calm. We have listened all night and it is the most beautiful thing. We are going to keep the array on. We are going to keep

message.oldrepublic.story.c5.helm: You take the helm and fly her yourself. She answers like an old friend with opinions.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.orbit: The sky thins to black and the stars stop twinkling. You are in orbit.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.jump: Starlines, a long breath of nothing, then a new sky. Your first jump from orbit.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.matriarch: The sand boils. The matriarch rises with her brood around her.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.honour: Varra raises her cup. "The debt for Torvin is paid. Clan Hask will deal with you."
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.honour_agai: You yielded first. The champion will wait for you to try again.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.debt.force: The debtor bolts, shouting for his friends. The salvagers reach for their weapons.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.debt.fight: The salvagers close in around the strongbox.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.debt.pay: You count out two hundred credits. The debtor stares at them, hands over the strongbox and walks off into the canyon.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.debt.run: The debtor shoulders the strongbox and runs. Now you need a story Ommo Teel will believe.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.debt.box: The strongbox is yours. Take it to Ommo Teel at Saltgate.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.cargo_faile: The patrol has your crate's signature. The job is void; Teel will offer it again.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.audience_re: Teel's jobs are done. Vessba the Hutt will grant you an audience.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.way.kajidic: The kajidic has sold the factor out. Dask's counting-house is open to you.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.way.clan: Clan Hask will break into the counting-house beside you.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.way.force: The way into the counting-house is open.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.door.trick: The doorman blinks, smiles, and holds the door for you. He will not remember why.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.door.fear: The guards look at you, then at each other, and find somewhere else to be.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.door.push: The door slams inward off its hinges. Behind it, the guards reach for their weapons.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.helmet: Varra turns the helmet over in her hands, then sets it at her side. "Clan iron comes home." The clan will remember.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.clan_hired: Varra's fighters fuel up. The next time you jump into Tyrvann's orbit, the clan flies with you.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.counting_ho: The counting-house guards stand aside. The stairs to Dask's office are clear.
An alarm whoops through the counting-house. Dask's enforcers come running.
Clan Hask's warriors kick in the side door beside you. Dask's enforcers come running.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.dask.releas: Dask nods once, gathers his coat and leaves by the back stair. By dawn his ship is gone.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.dask.clan: Varra's warriors take Dask by the arms. He goes quietly. He was always going to.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.dask.end: Dask's ledger ends on the floor of his own office.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.coordinates: Dask's data is in your nav: Tyrvann's coordinates, and the pattern Ulvaine's blockade flies.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.cannons: The shipwright bolts a pair of laser cannons under your wings. "Paid for out of the factor's ledger. Don't tell me how."
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.no_ship: The shipwright needs a ship to fit.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.ship_busy: Your ship is busy. Land it first.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.blockade_fa: Your ship limps away from Tyrvann. The blockade holds, for now.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.clan_help: The blockade is too strong to break alone. Varra Hask could bring the clan, for %s credits of fuel and missiles.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.blockade_pa: The interceptors hail "the singer" and peel away. The gunship lets you through.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.stones_dorr: Dorrun has marked the three verse stones on your map.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.stones_dask: Dask's data marks three places on Tyrvann where the storm sings: the verse stones.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.ending.spar: Ulvaine drops her saber. "The Hymn will outlast us both." She walks out into the storm, and the engine falls silent behind her.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.ending.bind: Ulvaine rises with her hands bound. She does not look back at the engine.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.ending.end: A short, unshowy end in the dark of the engine.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.helper_rewa: You helped bring down Darth Ulvaine.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.helper_done: You have already helped against Ulvaine today.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.complete: Chapter Five is complete. The Long Hymn waits beneath the Heart.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.cipher.ghes: The fence slots a cipher into the feed. Today's bounty on the Saltgate board shuffles.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.cipher.tyrv: The fence slots a cipher into the feed. Today's bounty on the holdfast board shuffles.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.shard_bough: The fence unwraps a hymnstone shard from oilcloth. It hums against your palm.
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.req.helmet: You do not carry Kaast's helmet
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.req.cipher_: The cipher has been used today
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.req.bounty_: That board's bounty is already taken today
message.oldrepublic.story.c5.req.trusted: Requires Trusted standing with the Vessba Kajidic
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.called: Find the factor who is asking after me: fly to Saltgate, on Ghessar
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.closed_gh: Ghessar is not on this server's charts. The way to the factor is closed.
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.saltgate: Reach the factor's counting-house: the kajidic's way, the clan's way or the Force's way
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.dask: Face Imrel Dask at the top of his counting-house
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.armed: Have the Saltgate shipwright fit cannons to my ship
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.closed_ty: Tyrvann is not on this server's charts. The way on is closed.
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.blockade: Break Ulvaine's blockade: jump into Tyrvann's orbit
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.not_ready: I am not ready for the Hymnal (level %s). Contracts and bounties give XP fastest.
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.hymnal: Face Darth Ulvaine in the Hymnal (level %s recommended)
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.report.in: Hold the journal and tell the Compass
quest.oldrepublic.c5.objective.complete: Chapter Five complete. The Long Hymn waits beneath the Heart.
quest.oldrepublic.c5.step.kajidic: The kajidic's way: Ommo Teel's jobs, %s/%s
quest.oldrepublic.c5.step.kajidic_audien: The kajidic's way: Vessba will see me
quest.oldrepublic.c5.step.clan: The clan's way: hunt the matriarch for Varra Hask
quest.oldrepublic.c5.step.clan_honour: The clan's way: answer for Kaast in a duel of honour, then hunt the matriarch
quest.oldrepublic.c5.step.force: The Force's way: the counting-house door
quest.oldrepublic.c5.step.clan_help: Ask Varra Hask to fly in with the clan (%s credits)
quest.oldrepublic.c5.journal.loop: The Long Hymn each week, Ulvaine's echo each day, and contracts and bounties at Saltgate and the holdfast.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c5.kaast_named: Kaast named a Hutt's factor. Here he is.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c5.call.1: There is a docking notice in the Compass's hum. Saltgate, on Ghessar: a factor's ship, berthed under a false flag.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c5.call.2: I have no business knowing that. Neither do you. And yet.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c5.call.3: Somebody wants you sung, not killed. I would want to know why.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c5.report.spare: She walks the storm now. Roads cross twice; mind where hers goes.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c5.report.bind: The clan has her, paid in her own coin. There is a kind of music in that.
npc.oldrepublic.tessaly.c5.report.end: The song ends. Walk on, and listen for the next one.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.c5.report.spare: You let her go. Mercy is not the same as forgiveness, and you knew the difference. Good.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.c5.report.bind: The Watch has her. She will be heard, which is more than she ever offered anyone.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.c5.report.end: It is done, then. I will not tell you it was wrong. I will tell you to carry it carefully.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.c5.report.spare: You let her walk. Sentiment, or a long game? Show me which, in time.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.c5.report.bind: The Council has her, and the Council knows whose hand delivered her. That is worth more than her head.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.c5.report.end: Clean. Final. The Council will pretend to be shocked. I am not.
npc.oldrepublic.dorrun.c5.greet: My sister says you are worth the trouble. Your map has three new marks. Go and make the stones quiet.
npc.oldrepublic.hask_champion.c5.idle: Varra speaks for the clan. I only fight for it.
npc.oldrepublic.hask_champion.c5.begin: Blades up. When one of us yields, it is done.
npc.oldrepublic.hask_champion.c5.contrac: A bout for the board? Fine. Try not to bleed on my boots.
npc.oldrepublic.bartender.bark.0: What'll it be? Don't answer, it all comes out of the same bottle.
npc.oldrepublic.bartender.bark.1: Fights outside. The kajidic charges for broken furniture.
npc.oldrepublic.bartender.bark.2: Clan on the left, kajidic on the right. Stand in the middle at your own risk.
npc.oldrepublic.bartender.bark.3: There's a factor upstairs who pays well for news. Heard he's stopped paying.
npc.oldrepublic.hub.not_yours: They are not waiting for you.
npc.oldrepublic.kajidic_factor.name: Kajidic factor
item.oldrepublic.ulvaines_writ.desc: The Dark Council's writ for the hand that delivered Darth Ulvaine. A keepsake, and a deed.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_factor_ask: A Hutt's factor has been asking after me in the Outer Rim ports. Whoever hired the Mandalorian has not given up; they have only changed their tools. The factor works out of Saltgate, on Ghessar.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_helm.title: The Helm
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_helm.body: I flew my ship by hand for the first time. She pulls a little to port and complains about it.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.saltgate.title: Saltgate
journal.oldrepublic.entry.saltgate.body: A walled port of sand-scoured prefab and old freighter hulls. Vessba the Hutt owns the pads, the walls, the water and the debts. Everyone who lands here walks on her sand.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_kajidic_wa: I did the kajidic's chores, and Vessba sold me the factor. "Dask's coin is good. Mine is better."
I hunted Clan Hask's matriarch in the dunes. The clan will break into Dask's counting-house beside me.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_forces_way: The counting-house door was shut. Then it was not.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_factor.bod: Imrel Dask kept the Buyer's ledger. He gave me Tyrvann's coordinates and the pattern of the blockade over it, and I decided what happened to him.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_buyers_fac: The Buyer has a face now, and a name: Darth Ulvaine. She wants me alive, because my Resonance makes stones sing, and something under Tyrvann's storms needs a singer.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.dask_ended.bod: Dask's ledger ended on the floor of his own office. The kajidic will not forget whose hand closed it.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.teeth.title: Teeth
journal.oldrepublic.entry.teeth.body: The Saltgate shipwright fitted a pair of laser cannons to my ship, paid for out of the factor's ledger. The blockade will not let a courier through politely.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_blockade.b: I broke Ulvaine's blockade over Tyrvann: the interceptors scattered and the gunship burned. The way down is open.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.tyrvann.title: Tyrvann
journal.oldrepublic.entry.tyrvann.body: A world of endless storm: stormwood, black mire and basalt ridges that call the lightning down. Clan Hask camps here, and something under the storm is singing.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.verse_one.body: I silenced a verse stone. In the quiet I saw a Sith with ink on his hands, writing music that made the stone weep: the First Cantor, composing the Hymn.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.verse_two.body: The second stone went quiet. I saw a choir of bound singers, their voices held in the stone long after their bodies had gone.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.verse_three.bo: The last stone fell silent. I saw the Hymn sung over a city, and the city falling quiet street by street until nothing sang but the stone.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_hymnal.bod: A sunken temple in the basalt ridges, its arch forever under lightning. The Heart's door opened for me.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.ulvaine_spared: I spared Darth Ulvaine. She dropped her saber and walked out into the storm, and the engine fell silent behind her.
I bound Darth Ulvaine and handed her over. She will answer for the Hymn, and sing for no one.
I ended Darth Ulvaine in the dark of the engine. A short, unshowy end.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.report_c5.body: I told my mentor how it ended in the Hymnal. The singer they were hunting is still singing.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_fall_offer: An acolyte came from Overseer Sorn with an offer. I have stopped pretending, he says. So has he.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.a_gift_for_the: I carried the Watch's holocron from the Greenwatch to the Proving and put it in Overseer Kaddor's hands.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_last_lesso: Master Saelen came to me. She knew. We fought, and she yielded, and I decided what that meant.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.kneel.title: Kneel
journal.oldrepublic.entry.kneel.body: I knelt before Overseer Sorn and rose a Sith.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_return_off: An apprentice came from the Greenwatch. Master Saelen says the door was never locked.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.amends.title: Amends
journal.oldrepublic.entry.amends.body: I freed three Republic prisoners from an Imperial detention post and flew them to the Greenwatch.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_overseers_: Overseer Sorn came to collect what I owed him. We fought, and he yielded, and I decided what that meant.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.welcomed.title: Welcomed
journal.oldrepublic.entry.welcomed.body: Master Saelen welcomed me into the Watch. She did not ask where I had been.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.master.title: Master
journal.oldrepublic.entry.master.body: The Council on Tython named me a Master of the Order. The first thing a Master learns is how little that changes.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.darth.title: Darth
journal.oldrepublic.entry.darth.body: The Dark Council's writ named me Darth. I chose the name myself.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.wayfarer.title: Wayfarer
journal.oldrepublic.entry.wayfarer.body: Tessaly Arn's echo gave me her mantle at Courier's Fall. The road was always mine.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_first_cant: Beneath the Heart, the First Cantor rose from his engine and sang the Long Hymn. We silenced him, for a week at least.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.space.title: Space
journal.oldrepublic.codex.space.body: Above every world, the orbit: black sky, slow stars and nothing to land on. A ship reaches it by climbing past the clouds, and jumps from it to other systems. Free flight is the pilot's own work; the autopilot only knows the safe roads.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.ghessar.title: Ghessar
journal.oldrepublic.codex.ghessar.body: A desert world of dunes, salt flats and red canyons on the Outer Rim. Sandstorms come up without warning. The Hutts keep their business here, and their sand.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.tyrvann.title: Tyrvann
journal.oldrepublic.codex.tyrvann.body: A storm-wrapped world of stormwood forests, black mires and basalt ridges where lightning never stops. Few land here on purpose.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.the_vessba_kaj: The Hutt crime family that owns Saltgate: Vessba the Hutt, her majordomo Ommo Teel, her harbourmaster and the enforcers who keep the port's peace for a price. They broker anything, including contracts on people.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.clan_hask.body: A Mandalorian clan of hunters and pilots, a few dozen warriors under the huntmaster Dorrun Hask, camped on Tyrvann. Torvin Kaast was one of theirs until he left to hunt alone. The clan judges deeds, not orders.
A voice on the Dark Council's edges, until she started asking for things the Council would not give her. Now she buys them. She found something under Tyrvann's storms that needs a singer.
A Sith composition older than the Treaty: music that binds those who sing it to the stone that holds it. The verse stones of Tyrvann sing it still.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.the_first_cant: The Sith who wrote the Long Hymn and bound a choir of singers into it. He sleeps inside the song-engine beneath the Hymnal's Heart, and wakes for anyone strong enough to call him.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.hymn_intercept: Ulvaine's fighters: black and violet blade-winged craft with engines that sing. They attack in pairs, fast and from above, and break away before you can turn.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.hymnsworn.body: Ulvaine's chanters, blades and storm-callers. While any of them lives, the stone they guard keeps singing. The storm-callers mark the ground before the lightning falls: watch for crawling static.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.sand_scours.bo: Ghessar's burrowing hunters. A ripple and a hiss in the sand is all the warning you get before one bursts out. They only take damage above ground.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.stormbacks.bod: Tyrvann's great grazers, harmless until provoked. Lightning seeks them out; a charged stormback hits harder, and its plates crackle with stolen storm.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.cartel_enforce: The kajidic's gunmen, bruisers and captains. They keep Saltgate's peace for whoever pays the kajidic, and their mood follows your standing with it.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.starfighters.b: Fighters live and die in orbit. Their shields recharge if you let them; their hulls do not. Nothing they carry survives the fall.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.force_stasis.b: A Jedi's way to take one dangerous enemy out of a fight for a few seconds, without hurting it.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.force_valor.bo: A Master's rallying power: a short window of courage for the caster and every ally near.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.force_drain.bo: The Sith way to endure: take life and Force from a living enemy.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.force_fear.bod: Break a group's nerve. The frightened run, and some doors open.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.force_rage.bod: A Darth's surrender to fury: harder, faster blows, at a price.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.mind_trick.bod: A weak mind stops fighting, or agrees with you. The strong-willed, the droids and the beasts do not.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.dual_blades.bo: A saber in each hand: the off hand strikes between the main hand's blows. Harder to master than it looks.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.legendary_comp: Schematics for parts no ordinary bench can make: rare lenses, pommels and ship parts. Each wants its discipline at level 5 and materials from the far worlds.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.the_spindle.bo: A Republic listening station from the old wars, gone quiet in the home system's orbit. Its last log speaks of a note from the storm, then forty voices, then a woman who only needed them to listen.
vision.oldrepublic.verse_one.1: A hand stained with ink writes music no throat could sing.
vision.oldrepublic.verse_one.2: "Let every voice on this world learn one song," says the Cantor.
vision.oldrepublic.verse_one.3: Under his pen, the stone begins to weep.
vision.oldrepublic.verse_two.1: A hundred singers kneel in rows, mouths open, eyes shut.
vision.oldrepublic.verse_two.2: Their voices pour into the stone and do not come back.
vision.oldrepublic.verse_two.3: Long after the singers are gone, the singing goes on.
vision.oldrepublic.verse_three.1: The Hymn rolls over a city of pale roofs.
vision.oldrepublic.verse_three.2: Street by street, the people stop speaking, and listen, and obey.
vision.oldrepublic.verse_three.3: At the end, nothing sings but the stone.
